newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slightly up on back of credit figures.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slightly up on back of credit figures.

text.p: Irish bonds were slightly up in thin late trade on Friday as fears of another retail rate rise in Ireland eased a touch after the release of key private sector credit growth figures, dealers said.
End-month banking statistics released on Thursday showed that private sector credit grew by 13.7 percent in July, up from 13.3 percent in June.
The growth rate was in line with market expectations, most of which were in the 13.5 to 14.0 percent range.
As July was the sixth consecutive month to see an increase in the overall growth rates some analysts felt one "must be prepared for the unexpected" as far as interest rate movements were concerned.

"Recent central bank activity in the money markets doesn't really seem to suggest that we're in for another retail rate rise but you cannot be sure. At face value it looks like the central bank are happy enough with where rates are at the moment but you never can tell," one dealer said.
In the UK, gilts recaptured strong tone again after dipping briefly on the back of U.S. payrolls data for July.
The payrolls data came in above market expectations at 250,000 and a subsequent rebound in U.S. treasury levels helped buoy the London market.
In the domestic market the eight percent bond due 2000 was up five pence from Thursday's close at 103.60 to yield 6.84 percent. The 10-year bond was up three pence at 102.65 to yield 7.46 percent.
Key one-month money market rates were unchanged from Thursday's close at 5.56/5.69 after rising temporarily in mid-morning trade.
